_note: The blocks and items, read by both editions. Ids are the save format: never change one, and never use one again for something else. Other blocks are named by their keys (see blockKey in index.html / DataKeys.cs).

_notes.BASE: the blocks and items written out one by one (the families, like torches, water and the coloured blocks, come later in this file), in the order the game defines them. id; name; pictures = the picture on every side, or [side, top, bottom] ([side, top, bottom, front] for blocks with a front); transparent = you can see through it; noCollide = you walk through it; shape = how it's drawn when it isn't a plain cube (half: a bottom slab; flat: lying on the ground; pieces: the 8 spots of cut pieces); box = the part you aim at and hit, [x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2] inside the block; drop = what breaking it gives (left out: itself, if it's in the inventory); handDrop = [thing, fewest, most] broken by hand; item = carried, not placed as a block; places = the block an item puts down; food = quarter hearts eating it heals; tool, material and damage = what a tool is, what it's made of and its hit; needs = the tool you must hold to break it in survival (axe or pickaxe); shovel = a shovel is the right tool (dug by hand it comes up as 1-8 pieces); leaves = leaves (a hoe cuts them, and they take the climate's colour); sound = how it sounds dug, walked on or put down (left out: stone); inventory = a block you can have in your inventory (it gives itself when broken, unless it has a drop); look = another look of the block it drops, put down at random in its place; log = a tree's log, standing (lying ones count through their drop: tree felling, and the stages an axe takes); fruit = what leaves drop now and then (1 in 4, broken without a hoe); sapling = the sapling leaves drop now and then (numbers.json SAPLING dropChance, broken without a hoe); grows = a sapling: the tree it grows into (oak, fir, palm, willow, or a worldgen.json TREE_SHAPES tree); sand = a sapling that can be planted on Sand too; plants = a seed: the crop it puts down on tilled soil with nothing on it (planting comes before eating); returns = what's left in your hand after eating it (a Jug of Milk: the Clay Jug); bag = a bag: one to a slot, it holds a mix of things up to one full stack (numbers.json STACK_MAX) in all, each thing taking STACK_MAX / its own stack size (so a tool or anything else one to a slot fills it); not another bag, nor anything holding things; full = a bag's picture while it holds anything (725, the Linen Utility Belt before it was dropped, is never used again)
_notes.KILN: the Kiln (73-80): 73-76 unlit, 77-80 lit (burning). Each faces one way: front = [x, z], the way its front picture faces; facing = which of the 4 (0-3, in that order); lit = burning; icon = its picture in the hotbar and inventory. The code finds them by number: 73 + facing (+ 4 when lit)
_notes.TORCHES: torches, one block for each wall and count: lit 22-41, smoldering 81-92, burnt 170-181, Ever Torches 182-193. shape torch = drawn as thin sticks; wall = [x, z], the way to the wall it leans off (null: standing); wi = which wall (0 standing, 1-4 in the order of the code's TORCH_WALLS); count = how many torches in the spot (lit 1-4; the others 1-4 standing, 1-2 on a wall); burn = 0 lit, 1 smoldering, 2 burnt, 3 Ever Torch. The code finds them by (burn, wi, count); it knows each burn's standing x1 by number (22, 81, 170, 182), and a lit x1 on wall wi is 22 + wi
_notes.WATER: water (50-57): level 0 is still water (seas, lakes, water you put down); 1-7 is flowing water, a step weaker for each block it has run. liquid = you swim in it. The code finds them by number: 50 + level
_notes.LYING_LOGS: logs lying down (360-375; the newer woods' are in WOODS), two for each log: axis 1 lies along x, 2 along z, with the log's name and pictures; drop = the log, which is how the game finds a log's lying ones (and breaking one gives it)
_notes.SNOW: snow lying in layers (380-386): layers = how many eighths of a block deep (1-7; 380 + layers - 1). You sink into the first layer (noCollide); 8 layers is a Snow Block
_notes.TOOLS: tools, 5 for each material in the order axe, pickaxe, shovel, sword, hoe: stone 207-211, then copper, iron, bronite, rosium and steel from 644 (the material's first + the kind's place). tool = which kind; material = what it's made of (its wear is numbers.json DURABILITY); damage = how much a hit takes off a mob. Tools don't stack
_notes.DEEP_STONE: the deep layers' stone (640-tall worlds have a new layer of stone every 64 blocks down from sea level): Stone (113-119), Cobblestone (121-127), Stone Bricks (128-134) and Chiseled Stone (135-141), each for layers 2-8. layer = which one (the plain blocks are layer 1); deeper is darker and harder to mine. The code finds them by number: the kind's first + layer - 2
_notes.SOILS: tilled soil (93-96): soil = it's tilled; wet = water is near; fert = fertilized with Bone Ash. The code finds them by number: 93, + 1 if wet, + 2 if fertilized
_notes.GRAIN: Grain growing (42-49): stage = 0-7 (7 is ripe), the code's GRAIN_STAGES in order
_notes.COLOURS: the 12 colours' Dyes (items 600-611) and, for each colour but red (whose blocks are in BASE), its Terracotta (218-228), Chiseled Terracotta (229-239) and Bricks (240-250). The code finds a colour's blocks by its place in the colours' list
_notes.METALS: the four metals' Ores (142-145), Chunks (630-633) and Bricks (634-637). pick = how good a pickaxe it takes to mine (numbers.json's PICK_TIER)
_notes.DEEP_ORES: each ore in each deeper layer (470-497): 470 + 7 x the ore's place (copper, iron, gold, tin) + layer - 2. Named, mined (pick) and dropping like the ore, but a Chunk for each layer down
_notes.FOUNDRY: the Foundry's Furnace (151-158): like the Kiln, 151 + facing (+ 4 when lit)
_notes.GEAR: armor, backpacks and utility belts, one of each per tier (leather, copper, iron, bronite, rosium, steel; material = the tier). Armor is 669 + 4 x tier + armor (0 helmet, 1 chestplate, 2 leggings, 3 boots); its wear is numbers.json ARMOR_DURABILITY. Backpacks are 693 + tier (pack = the slots it adds); utility belts are 699 + tier (belt = its offhand slots, tools = its tool slots)
_notes.FLOWERS: flowers (194-198): shape plant = the picture twice, crossed like an X; dye = the Dye it makes. The code finds them in its flower colours' order
_notes.SNOWY: blocks with a layer of snow in their space too (a torch, a flower, pieces, the Cutter, a Rock, Clay Ball or Brick put down): each is the block it holds (inner) with snowed = 1, and any fields of its own (here: what breaking it gives, and the box: at least as high as the snow). From 400: the torches and flowers in id order; 388 pieces, 389 the Cutter, 390-392 a Rock, Clay Ball and Brick
_notes.WOODS: the woods of the Trees and Leaves update. First the fruit (3610-3612). Then each wood at 2200 + 100 x its place (cedar, maple, birch, aspen, redwood, cherry, cypress, juniper, larch, holly, orange, palo verde): + 0 log, + 1 stripped log, + 2 planks, + 3 leaves, + 4 and + 5 the log lying along x and z, + 6 and + 7 the stripped log lying, + 8 its sapling, + 10, 20, 30 and 40 the log's, stripped log's, planks' and leaves' forms (see FORMS), + 50 its door (the item; the doors put down are in DOORS). Then the Dead Log (3600; lying 3601-3602) and the older woods' doors (3400 oak, 3440 fir, 3480 palm, 3520 willow) and saplings (3560 oak, 3561 fir, 3562 palm, 3563 willow; the Dead tree has none)
_notes.CROPS: crops growing (3700-3721; Grain is GRAIN): crop = which crop, stage = 0-3 (3 is ripe), top = Corn's upper block (stages 2 and 3 only; it breaks with the bottom and only the bottom grows). Potato 3700-3703, Turnip 3704-3707, Flax 3708-3711, Corn 3712-3715 (the bottom; tops 3716-3717), Cantaloupe Vine 3718-3721. drop = what an unripe one gives (its seed back); a ripe one gives its harvest (numbers.json CROPS). The code finds them by crop and stage. Wild crops (worldgen.json WILD_CROPS) are the ripe stage standing on natural ground: they never grow, since only tilled soil grows a crop
_notes.FENCES: fences (3760-3775), one per wood in the doors' order: of = the planks they're made of (their picture); shape fence = a post 4/16 square the block's height, and two rails to each neighbour it joins (a fence, a door, or a whole solid block you can't see through), worked out when it's drawn (nothing extra is saved). You can't jump one (it stands 1.5 high to players), and no mob hops one
_notes.DOORS: the doors as they stand: of = the planks it's made of (its edges look like them), item = the door you carry, first = its first state. Each door has 32, numbered first + facing x 8 + hinge x 4 + open x 2 + half, which the game makes: facing = the way its front faces (the Kiln's numbers), hinge 0 = on the left as you look at its front, 1 = on the right, open 0 or 1, half 0 = the bottom, 1 = the top. The big faces show <item>_bottom or <item>_top (hinge on the right: mirrored)
_notes.FORM_NAMES: the forms a block can be cut into, in order, and what each is called (an item is named "<the block> <this>", like Oak Planks Slab)
_notes.FORMS: the blocks that can be cut (in the order the Shapes tab and the Cutter show them) and the item for each of its forms (see FORM_NAMES): a Piece (an eighth of the block), Slab, Vertical Slab... Each item has its block's pictures and is named after it
_notes.EARTH_GROUND: Earthlike's grounds (Earthly Extravaganza; earthlike = hidden until the Earthlike release: not in your inventory, the creative inventory, search or recipes, and only Earthlike's land puts them down): the sub-biomes' grounds (3920-3939; 3932, 3933 and 3936 stay spare) and the Burnt Log (3994; lying 3995 along x, 3996 along z)
_notes.EARTH_PLANTS: Earthlike's plants (3940-3961; earthlike as in EARTH_GROUND): shape plant = crossed like the flowers; top = a two-tall plant's upper block (it breaks with the lower one, which is the one you carry); tint = takes the climate's colour; water = it stands in still water (its space counts as still water too)
_notes.EARTH_ROCKS: Earthlike's rocks (earthlike as in EARTH_GROUND): Geology Draft 2's 11 rocks (4400 + n: Limestone, Shale, Chalk, Granite, Basalt, Gabbro, Slate, Schist, Gneiss, Marble, Quartzite), their cobbled forms (4420 + n), bricks (4440 + n) and polished forms (4460 + n; Polished Andesite 4471); the ores in them (4480-4492; in = the rock an ore is in, so it has its own key) and Laterite (4494); the erosion draft's 10 rocks (4760 + n: Conglomerate, Siltstone, Dolomite, Travertine, Diorite, Rhyolite, Peridotite, Phyllite, Serpentinite, Hornfels), cobbled (4770 + n), polished (4780 + n), bricks (4790 + n); Flint Nodules (4820) and the Flint they drop (726). Breaking a rock gives its cobbled form. Since Beta 0.1.5.2 the 21 rocks, their cobbled, bricks and polished forms (and Polished Andesite) are shown (no earthlike), and land 7 and 8's rock blobs put Geology Draft 2's 11 rocks down in every other world type; the ores in them, Laterite, Flint Nodules and Flint stay hidden
_notes.EARTH_SOILS: Earthlike's soils (4800-4809: Prairie Soil, Ashen Soil, Red Earth, Loess, Desert Soil, Clay Soil, Sandy Soil, Stony Soil, Volcanic Soil, Glacial Till) and their grassy tops (4810 + the same n; Desert Soil has none); earthlike as in EARTH_GROUND
_notes.EARTH_GRAVELS: a gravel for each rock (5030 + n, in EARTH_ROCKS' order, then Sandstone's at 5051; Andesite's is today's Gravel); falls = it falls like Sand; shown since Beta 0.1.5.2 (no earthlike), but only Earthlike's land puts them down
_notes.EARTH_WOODS: Earthlike's woods (earthlike as in EARTH_GROUND), each at 4000 + 100 x its place (Mahogany, Acacia, Stiltroot, Teak), laid out as WOODS': + 0 log, + 1 stripped log, + 2 planks, + 3 leaves, + 4 / + 5 the log lying along x / z, + 6 / + 7 the stripped log lying, + 8 sapling, + 50 the door you carry (+ 51-82 its states: EARTH_DOORS); + 10-46 the forms (EARTH_FORMS)
_notes.EARTH_FENCES: the Earthlike woods' fences (3776-3779), as FENCES; earthlike as in EARTH_GROUND
_notes.RIVER_WATER: running river water (Earthlike; earthlike as in EARTH_GROUND): 3891 + 8 x pace + flow; flow = the way it runs (0-7: E, SE, S, SW, W, NW, N, NE; 8 falling), pace = 0 gentle, 1 quick, 2 rapids (3915 falling: flow 8, pace 2). It counts as still water everywhere water does, and is a source that never changes on its own
_notes.EARTH_DOORS: the Earthlike woods' doors, as DOORS; earthlike as in EARTH_GROUND
_notes.EARTH_FORMS: the Earthlike blocks that can be cut, as FORMS (the woods' earthlike as in EARTH_GROUND; the rocks' shown since Beta 0.1.5.2): the woods' (+ 10-46), then the rocks' (4500 + 7 x n for Geology Draft 2's 36 rows, n in EARTH_ROCKS' order: rocks, cobbled, bricks (row 25, 4675-4681, spare), polished with Polished Andesite last; then 4830 + 7 x n for the erosion draft's 28 (row 22, 4984-4990, spare))
